correctness.rationale: The only nontrivial rank minors impose ad=ae=af=bf=df=0 and be=cd, and the only possible nonzero commutator coordinates impose symmetry of a_i d_j, d_i f_j and a_i e_j+b_i f_j. On the locus where the d-vector is nonzero, the first two symmetry conditions and the rank equations force all a and f to vanish; its closure is the product of the rank-one 2-by-2 cones. On d=0, at each position at most one of x=(a,b), y=(e,f) is nonzero. If both types occur then their spans are perpendicular lines; all zero-type indices can be assigned arbitrarily, proving the mixed-component cover. For fixed labeled S the incidence vector bundle has rank 2t over P^1, projection is closed, and a mixed tuple recovers the common line, giving dimension 2t+1. A witness for M_S is obtained with every x_i=(1,0) on S and y_j=(0,1) off S; this lies in no other listed locus, even in characteristic two. The two homogeneous affine spaces have dimension 3t, and choosing a nonzero a or f separates each from all others; d≠0 separates the determinantal product. This proves completeness and applies at t=1 with no M_S. Finite-field counts split into the product contribution (q^3+q^2−q)^t−(2q^2−q)^t on d≠0, and q^t times [2q^{2t}−1+(q+1)((2q−1)^t−2q^t+1)] on d=0. The latter counts both homogeneous types once at their overlap, and each mixed tuple via its unique rational projective line. Fresh literal rank-minor and full-product enumeration gives 212, 2601, 2088 for (q,t)=(2,2),(3,2),(2,3), and checks the cover for (2,2),(2,3). The finite regressions are not used instead of the all-field proof.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns the reduced variety with labeled positions, not unreduced schemes, simultaneous conjugacy, or higher ranks/sizes.
